raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On ROCm, `CustomAllreduce.should_custom_ar()` only selects the custom all-reduce when the GPUs are fully connected by XGMI or the deterministic 1-stage kernel is enabled. Without either, `__init__` still allocates the meta/data buffers and exports IPC handles, although the result is never used.

That setup fails when `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`: `self.buffer` comes from the caching allocator, so it is VMM-backed (`hipMemCreate`/`hipMemMap`), and `hipIpcGetMemHandle` on it returns `invalid argument`. `CUDACHECK` then calls `exit()`, so the process dies during distributed init. The SGLang Diffusion CI cases for MiniMax-H3 set this allocator option.

Observed with SGLang Diffusion, MiniMax-H3 t2va, TP2 on two PCIe Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201):

```
Failed: Cuda error .../csrc/allreduce/custom_all_reduce.hip:152 'invalid argument'
```

Single-GPU check of the failing call (`sgl_kernel.allreduce.get_meta_buffer_ipc_handle`):

| buffer | `hipIpcGetMemHandle` |
|---|---|
| `hipMalloc` / `hipExtMallocWithFlags` (default, fine-grained, uncached, contiguous) | ok |
| `torch.empty`, `expandable_segments:False` | ok |
| `torch.empty`, `expandable_segments:True` | `invalid argument` |

## Modifications

- `CustomAllreduce.__init__`: on ROCm, when the GPUs are not fully XGMI-connected and the deterministic implementation is off, return early as disabled. `should_custom_ar()` returns `False` in this case anyway, so the selected all-reduce (RCCL) does not change; only the unused IPC setup is skipped.
- New CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce_rocm_topology.py`: the IPC setup is skipped without XGMI, and still runs with full XGMI and/or the deterministic implementation. The skip case fails without this change.

XGMI-connected Instinct GPUs and the deterministic path are unchanged.

## Open question for maintainers (Instinct)

I could only test on PCIe RDNA4. On XGMI-connected Instinct GPUs the custom all-reduce is actually used, so the same `hipIpcGetMemHandle` call on `torch.empty(...)` should hit the same error if `expandable_segments:True` is set, and so would `register_buffer(inp)` in the deterministic path and graph buffer registration. Could someone with MI300X/MI355X confirm? If it reproduces, possible fixes are allocating `self.buffer` outside the expandable segments, or a shareable-handle path like #27593 does for CUDA (`hipMemExportToShareableHandle`). I kept this PR to the PCIe case.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerical change: on the affected configurations the custom all-reduce was never selected. TP2 on 2x R9700 (PCIe), ROCm 7.15, `expandable_segments:True`. gfx1201 is not a supported `sgl-kernel` target yet, so `sgl-kernel` was built with the allowlist / wave32 changes of `docker/patches/sgl-kernel-gfx1151.sh` retargeted to gfx1201; the code path changed here is architecture-independent.

| | `CustomAllreduce` init | all-reduce used | MiniMax-H3 t2va TP2, 1 step, `torch_sdpa` |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | process exits (`custom_all_reduce.hip:152 'invalid argument'`) | - | fails at init |
| this PR | disabled, logs the reason | RCCL | runs, video saved |

2-GPU check with `SGLANG_ENABLE_DETERMINISTIC_INFERENCE=1` and `expandable_segments:False`: init and `should_custom_ar() == True` as before.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: no kernel or dispatch change. It only removes an unused allocation of `meta_size() + max_size` (uncached) plus `2 * max_size` bytes per rank, and the IPC handle exchange at init.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

nodes.body:
@yizhang2077 @merrymercy @ch-wan (CODEOWNERS of `srt/distributed`) @HaiShaw (ROCm): could one of you take a look and trigger CI (`/tag-and-rerun-ci`)? I am not in `CI_PERMISSIONS.json`.

The change only affects ROCm setups where `should_custom_ar()` can never select the custom all-reduce (not fully XGMI-connected and deterministic mode off); it skips the unused IPC setup that currently crashes with `expandable_segments:True`. XGMI-connected Instinct GPUs and the deterministic path are unchanged. The open question in the description (whether the same `hipIpcGetMemHandle` failure hits MI300X/MI355X with `expandable_segments:True`) needs someone with Instinct hardware.

@Shan2L Thanks for flagging this. Short answer: **yes, it reproduces on XGMI-connected Instinct GPUs**, but only on SGLang's own `CustomAllreduce`. The default ROCm path, AITER's custom all-reduce, already handles it.

**Setup:** 8x gfx1250, fully XGMI-connected, ROCm 10 / HIP 7.15, PyTorch 2.11. This isn't an MI300X or MI355X, but the failure is in the HIP runtime (a VMM-backed pointer can't be exported through `hipIpcGetMemHandle`), so I expect the same behavior there. A quick check on MI300X/MI355X would still be welcome.

**1. Which buffers can be IPC-exported (single GPU):**

| buffer | `expandable_segments:False` | `expandable_segments:True` |
|---|---|---|
| `torch.empty` (any size, base or interior pointer) | ok | `invalid argument` |
| tensor allocated during CUDA graph capture | ok | `invalid argument` |
| `allocate_meta_buffer` (uncached `hipExtMallocWithFlags`) | ok | ok |
| raw `hipMalloc` | ok | ok |

**2. Your three suspicions, tested on 2 XGMI GPUs with `expandable_segments:True`:**

- **Init:** confirmed. `register_buffer(self.buffer)` fails at `custom_all_reduce.hip:152 'invalid argument'` and the process exits, in both deterministic and non-deterministic mode. This PR's early return only covers the non-XGMI case, so XGMI is still affected.
- **`register_buffer(inp)` in the deterministic path:** confirmed for inputs at or above `max_size`. Smaller inputs are copied into `self.buffer` first, so they only export that buffer. #34543 already removes this call: it reduces oversized inputs in `max_size` pieces through `self.buffer`. With #34543 plus an init fix, a 32 MiB deterministic all-reduce passes under `expandable_segments:True`.
- **Graph buffer registration:** confirmed on the non-deterministic SGLang path (`all_reduce_reg` during capture). Even with `self.buffer` allocated outside the caching allocator, `register_graph_buffers` fails at `custom_all_reduce_hip.cuh:535`, because the captured tensors are VMM-backed. Forcing the copy-in (unregistered) path during capture fixes it. Deterministic-mode capture only registers `self.buffer`, so it's fine once that buffer is exportable.

**3. Who is affected in practice:**

By default ROCm dispatches to AITER's `CustomAllreduce`, which already handles expandable segments (ROCm/aiter#4621): its IPC-exported buffers stay on plain `hipMalloc` memory and graph capture is forced to copy-in. On the same hardware, AITER init, eager all-reduce and graph replay all pass with `expandable_segments:True`.

SGLang's own implementation, and therefore this bug, is only used with:
- deterministic inference or `SGLANG_USE_1STAGE_ALLREDUCE=1`,
- `SGLANG_USE_AITER_AR=0`, or
- AITER not installed.

**4. Suggested follow-up (separate PR, after #34543 lands):**

1. Allocate `self.buffer` outside expandable segments, either by temporarily switching the allocator setting for that one allocation (verified to produce an exportable buffer) or with a plain-`hipMalloc` op. `allocate_meta_buffer` works, but its uncached memory would likely slow down the data buffer.
2. When expandable segments are enabled, force copy-in during graph capture on the non-deterministic path, mirroring the existing `tms_cudagraph` handling.
3. Re-run `test_amd_deterministic_custom_allreduce.py` (from #34543) and an eager-plus-graph 2-GPU test with `expandable_segments:True` as a regression test.

The shareable-handle route (`hipMemExportToShareableHandle`, as in #27593) would also work, but it's a bigger change than this needs. I think this PR is fine as-is for the PCIe case.

files.patch:
@@ -95,6 +95,15 @@ def __init__(
         if full_nvlink is None:
             return  # fail to get nvlink status
 
+        if _is_hip and full_nvlink is False and not self.use_amd_deterministic_impl:
+            # should_custom_ar() never selects this path, so skip the IPC setup,
+            # which also fails on expandable_segments (VMM) allocations.
+            logger.info(
+                "CustomAllreduce is disabled because the GPUs are not fully "
+                "connected by XGMI; all-reduce uses RCCL."
+            )
+            return
+
         self.group = group
         self.max_size = max_size
         self.rank = rank

@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+
+from sglang.srt.distributed.device_communicators import custom_all_reduce
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class _IpcSetupStarted(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+def _build(monkeypatch, *, full_xgmi, deterministic):
+    def allocate_meta_buffer(size):
+        raise _IpcSetupStarted
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(custom_all_reduce, "_is_hip", True)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        custom_all_reduce,
+        "ops",
+        SimpleNamespace(
+            IS_CUSTOM_AR_AVAILABLE=True,
+            meta_size=lambda: 0,
+            allocate_meta_buffer=allocate_meta_buffer,
+        ),
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        custom_all_reduce, "_use_amd_deterministic_impl", lambda: deterministic
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(custom_all_reduce.dist, "get_rank", lambda group: 0)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(custom_all_reduce.dist, "get_world_size", lambda group: 2)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        custom_all_reduce,
+        "can_use_custom_all_reduce_with_nvlink",
+        lambda **kwargs: full_xgmi,
+    )
+    return custom_all_reduce.CustomAllreduce(group=object(), device="cpu")
+
+
+def test_rocm_without_xgmi_skips_ipc_setup(monkeypatch):
+    ca = _build(monkeypatch, full_xgmi=False, deterministic=False)
+    assert ca.disabled
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("full_xgmi", "deterministic"), [(True, False), (False, True), (True, True)]
+)
+def test_rocm_usable_custom_ar_still_sets_up_ipc(monkeypatch, full_xgmi, deterministic):
+    with pytest.raises(_IpcSetupStarted):
+        _build(monkeypatch, full_xgmi=full_xgmi, deterministic=deterministic)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    import sys
+
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))

With #34543 plus an init fix, a 32 MiB deterministic all-reduce passes under `expandable_segments:True`.
- **Graph buffer registration:** confirmed on the non-deterministic SGLang path (`all_reduce_reg` during capture). Even with `self.buffer` allocated outside the caching allocator, `register_graph_buffers` fails at `custom_all_reduce_hip.cuh:535`, because the captured tensors are VMM-backed. Forcing the copy-in (unregistered) path during capture fixes it. Deterministic-mode capture only registers `self.buffer`, so it's fine once that buffer is exportable.

**3. Who is affected in practice:**

By default ROCm dispatches to AITER's `CustomAllreduce`, which already handles expandable segments (ROCm/aiter#4621): its IPC-exported buffers stay on plain `hipMalloc` memory and graph capture is forced to copy-in. On the same hardware, AITER init, eager all-reduce and graph replay all pass with `expandable_segments:True`.

SGLang's own implementation, and therefore this bug, is only used with:
- deterministic inference or `SGLANG_USE_1STAGE_ALLREDUCE=1`,
- `SGLANG_USE_AITER_AR=0`, or
- AITER not installed.

**4. Suggested follow-up (separate PR, after #34543 lands):**

1. Allocate `self.buffer` outside expandable segments, either by temporarily switching the allocator setting for that one allocation (verified to produce an exportable buffer) or with a plain-`hipMalloc` op. `allocate_meta_buffer` works, but its uncached memory would likely slow down the data buffer.
2. When expandable segments are enabled, force copy-in during graph capture on the non-deterministic path, mirroring the existing `tms_cudagraph` handling.
3. Re-run `test_amd_deterministic_custom_allreduce.py` (from #34543) and an eager-plus-graph 2-GPU test with `expandable_segments:True` as a regression test.

The shareable-handle route (`hipMemExportToShareableHandle`, as in #27593) would also work, but it's a bigger change than this needs. I think this PR is fine as-is for the PCIe case.


cc: @vvagaytsev

Validated on PCIe-connected RDNA4 (gfx1201 ×2, TP2).

- **Stack:** current `main` + #43679 (gfx1201 kernel build) + #47254 (RDNA default attention), with/without this PR.
- **Environment:** stock `rocm/pytorch` image with the `amdsmi` Python package installed, so the XGMI topology query actually runs. No aiter.
- **Workload:** Qwen/Qwen3-8B, `--tp-size 2`.

| | without this PR | with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| all-reduce log | `[AR] All-reduce call path: NCCL (custom AR disabled)` (the IPC setup still runs) | `CustomAllreduce is disabled because the GPUs are not fully connected by XGMI; all-reduce uses RCCL.` |
| gsm8k (sgl-eval, 100 questions) | 96% | 94% (within sampling noise at n=100) |
| bench_serving random-ids 512/256, c=1 | 40.73 tok/s, TPOT 24.30 ms | 40.71 tok/s, TPOT 24.32 ms |
| c=8 | 314.3 tok/s, TPOT 24.28 ms | 313.8 tok/s, TPOT 24.24 ms |

Behaviour and throughput are unchanged. On PCIe Radeon cards the all-reduce already went through RCCL; this PR just skips the unused IPC setup and says why in the log. LGTM from the RDNA side.

Unrelated to this PR: OLMoE-1B-7B with `--tp-size 2` fails at startup on this `main` stack in both arms (`ValueError: Expected hidden_size to be 2048, but found: 1024`). I'm looking into it separately.

Adding an RDNA3 data point to the earlier RDNA4 one. Setup:
- two W7900-class GPUs (gfx1100) over PCIe, TP2, Qwen3-8B;
- main plus #43679 (sgl-kernel build for RDNA), #47254 (RDNA attention default) and a vLLM `fused_add_rms_norm` call fix this environment needs;
- sgl-eval gsm8k, 100 questions; `bench_serving` random ids, 512 in / 256 out.

| | log | gsm8k | c1 / c8 / c32 tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | `custom AR disabled` | 94% | 39.8 / 282.9 / 845.4 |
| this PR | `... disabled because the GPUs are not fully connected by XGMI; all-reduce uses RCCL` | 96% | 39.7 / 282.7 / 844.6 |

Same as on RDNA4: the IPC setup is skipped and the reason is logged, with throughput unchanged.
